messages.author: 8ffd6137fd43c6df
messages.subject: Non-automatic vignette with devtools?
parts:
https://github.com/wibeasley/RVignetteExample

This is a minimal example of an R package that has a nonstandard vignette. I would like to have a working example of a vignette with these features:
  1. Is built with knitr instead of Sweave.
  2. Uses knitr's code externalization feature, where almost all the R code lives in a dedicated *.R file. I've added vignettes/CodeBehindVignette.R to .Rbuildignore, but I don't know if that's necessary.
  3. Is not rebuilt every time the package is checked. I am pretending this vignette takes a long time to run and compile, and should not be run on CRAN or win-builder computer (or even run on the developer's computer is they don't want to take 5+ minutes)
  4. Saves images to a dedicated directory to make it easier to track changes in GitHub. Presumably this directory is ./vignettes/FigureRmd, but the location doesn't really matter to me. I've added this folder to .Rbuildignore, but I'm not sure that's necessary.
I chose an Rmd file instead of a Rnw, so that it could be more portable and run on more development boxes, and increase the chance of getting a more helpful response. If these two types of files handles things differently, I'll add an Rnw example. I am intentionally not using knitr's caching mechanism, in case it makes package development and portability trickier.

I know there were a few tricks to keep the vignettes from being rebuilt automatically, such as placing a stub Rnw file in the inst/doc directory. But I'm not sure that's legal since R changed the file structure of vignettes (like splitting up the files in the ./vignettes/ and ./inst/doc/). Besides, I'd like to construct them in a consistent way with devtools, to reduce the chance for complications later. I wondering if devtools is planning to do this a different way than the Makefile approach described in R-exts.

Can someone specify a structure that would work naturally with devtools?  If there's an existing resource that describes this, I'd like to know about it. The “Package level documentation” chapter in Advanced R Programming looks like it was last updated before R 3.0 was released (because it doesn't mention knitr).  I've also looked at R-exts, knitr's vignette demo, and older sources like Leisch's 2009 tutorial.  The source for this vignette is on GitHub, and can be previewed here.

Thank you, Will Beasley

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Non-automatic vignette with devtools?
parts:
Hi Will,

I don't think there is a natural way to do this because you don't want
a lot of the standard features of vignettes. Rather than mostly
reinventing the wheel, I'd recommend that you think about how you
could get the most out of the existing vignette system, while getting
as many of the features as you want. Since you want to use code
externalisation, I'd suggest that you have two external files:

1) run manually, and included with eval = FALSE: that would perform
the computationally expensive work

2) run automatically, in the usual way

If it's possible to split up your work like this, I'd strongly
encourage you to do so. Otherwise you will be fighting a running
battle with CRAN, who really do want your vignettes to be run
automatically on ever test. Personally, I think that's a reasonable
thing to do - if you want other behaviour you can achieve it using
cached results, or otherwise don't use a vignette.

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: Non-automatic vignette with devtools?
parts:
Thanks Hadley, I don't think I understand the two files, but maybe I don't need to.  I'd rather have the ability to determine when the vignette built (instead of building during every build/check), than have and external code file.  Is there an approach that's natural to do this with devtools?  Or am I pushing the boundaries of the devtools forum, and should go to something like StackOverflow?

It was working exactly the way I wanted before they added the `vignettes/` directory.  But I haven't found an example that works with the new file structure.  My own attempts didn't work, and even got me scolded.

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Non-automatic vignette with devtools?
parts:
> Thanks Hadley, I don't think I understand the two files, but maybe I don't
> need to. I'd rather have the ability to determine when the vignette built
> (instead of building during every build/check), than have and external code
> file. Is there an approach that's natural to do this with devtools? Or am
> I pushing the boundaries of the devtools forum, and should go to something
> like StackOverflow?

It's not possible to do with devtools because (by and large) devtools
just provides convenient wrappers around existing R package
functionality. Building every time is very much a property of a
vignette, so fundamentally I think you want something that's not a
vignette (although clearly it's pretty similar). I think asking about
it on this mailing list is fine, although you might get more ideas on
SO.

> It was working exactly the way I wanted before they added the `vignettes/`
> directory. But I haven't found an example that works with the new file
> structure. My own attempts didn't work, and even got me scolded.

Yes, I think one of the reasons for the move to the new directory
structure is to prevent exactly what you're trying to do.

Hadley
